request.spec:
Selected claims can be moved to another person together: a select of the person and a button
beside the bulk buttons. Each selected claim is moved in list order by exactly the rules of moving
one claim (who may, which statuses, closed periods, retirement, with the same CLAIM_REASSIGNED and
rollup lines); each that cannot is left as it is. Show how many were moved and how many were
refused.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Selected claims can be moved to another person together: a select of the person and a button
beside the bulk buttons. Each selected claim is moved in list order by exactly the rules of moving
one claim (who may, which statuses, closed periods, retirement, with the same CLAIM_REASSIGNED and
rollup lines); each that cannot is left as it is. Show how many were moved and how many were
refused.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Bulk moving of claims is in, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

**How it works now:** beside the bulk Open and Settle buttons there's a "Move selected claims to" person select and a Move button. It shows "Moved N, refused M" (`bulk-reassigned` and `bulk-reassign-refused`). If no person is chosen, or the request fails, it shows an error (`bulk-reassign-error`).

**Behind it:** a new endpoint, `POST /api/sheets/{id}/claims/bulk-reassign` in `ClaimController.java`, built the same way as bulk open and settle:
- It takes the selected claims in list order and moves each one with the existing single-claim move, in its own transaction. So the same checks apply (role permission, DRAFT/OPEN/PENDING only, closed periods, retirement, corrections), and each move writes the same `CLAIM_REASSIGNED` and rollup lines.
- A claim that can't be moved is counted as refused and left untouched.
- For a viewer or an archived sheet, every selected claim is refused.

**One place it differs from moving a single claim:** the single move refuses a claim that already belongs to the chosen person. The test requires the bulk move to accept it: it expects Ben's own claim, moved to Ben, to count as moved and log `from=Ben to=Ben`. So `ClaimService.reassign` now has a version with a `bulk` flag that skips only that check. Such a claim is also re-listed as that person's newest. The screen updates its order only after the sheet is reloaded.

No database migration was needed.
